title: Supplication at Arete's Knees
part: The four books with no filmed scene (3, 7, 15, 20): Book 7's key scene, filmed for the first time
hypothesis: The scene is a stranger made visible and a hall struck silent. It reads if the mist is something on screen (LEGO: a column of trans clear and white round bricks carried on him up the hall, sinking into the floor at the queen's knees), if he is seen on his knees clasping hers through his prayer, and if the silence is the faces of the king, the queen and the lords held on him before the elder speaks; and if his prayer is said in a man's voice.

result: Kept as take 2. The camera is no longer inside a head at 42.6-43.2 s (the queen's close runs to 44.0 s, then the king's two-shot from outside the lords). Odysseus is seen on both knees at the queen's knees, his shins flat on the floor behind him, his body upright and his face up to hers, a hand on her knee, from low at the side of the thrones, for 2.0 s as he begins to pray and again for 1.6 s ('I come to your knees'); between them the lords start. Loose: the mist's sinking (6.7-8.4 s) is still seen high from behind the king's chair, his crown in the foreground; the kneel shots have the king's chair and a lord's shoulder at the edges; the hands are near, not exactly on, her knees (the left 10 units off on average); the king's hand-grip at 49-52 s does not meet (as in take 1); the prayer's mid (15.6 s) and close (20.8 s) are on his face, not his kneeling body.
